analysis: Examined ClusterOnboardingPairServing.swift (base and head) and ClusterService+RestartingStop.swift (patch, base and head). The RestartingStop change is comment-only (lines 5-8 head), documenting that the automatic stop is not counted as a person's stop via ClusterSetupRecord.stopsAsked. The pair-serving change adds three things to the onboarding UI helpers: ClusterOnboardingStopped.transferKeptLine (a constant string), ClusterOnboardingStopped.asked(since:now:) (a pure Int? comparison that returns false when either count is nil), and the new ClusterOnboardingFollowedStop struct (head lines 422-444), which holds only local Int? state and is mutated through look(_:begun:startStops:). None of it touches the network, a file, a key, an attestation or authorization path, or any of the coordinator-provider WebSocket, App Attest, cache, fan helper or add-on boundaries. The only security-adjacent concern is that a peer Mac's status could feed an attacker-influenced stopsAsked count. That could at most end the joining Mac's follow of the start early (a UI-level availability effect). The fail-safe direction holds: nil or non-increasing counts never signal a stop. Peer status is already within the cluster's trust assumptions (TB-011/TB-012 context and existing cluster onboarding), and no authorization decision rests on it. Integration questions for later passes: where the stopsAsked counter is incremented and persisted (ClusterSetupRecord, not supplied), whether the status carrying it is authenticated between Macs, and that automatic restarting stops (restoreStart, the replan paths) never increment it. That counter code is not in this batch, so the claim in the new comment (never counted as asked for) is unverified here. No regression identified in the supplied units.
